title: Basics of Computer Networks - GeeksforGeeks
description: Primer on what a network is, client-server versus peer-to-peer designs, and core hardware such as routers and switches. Plain language with little jargon, so it suits a first read.

title: Computer network
description: Wikipedia overview of network hardware, transmission media, and the history from packet switching and ARPANET to the modern Internet. Gives a broad undergraduate-level map of the field.

title: Network Topology - GeeksforGeeks
description: Explains physical versus logical topology and compares mesh, star, bus, ring, tree, hybrid and point-to-point layouts with their advantages and drawbacks.

title: RFC 1958: Architectural Principles of the Internet
description: IAB memo on the design principles behind the Internet, such as end-to-end intelligence, connectivity first, and simplicity. Advanced because it is a primary-source design rationale rather than a tutorial.

title: What is the OSI Model?
description: Cloudflare Learning Center walkthrough of the seven OSI layers and how data moves from one application down and up the stack. Short and example-driven, good for beginners.

title: OSI model
description: Wikipedia article on the seven-layer reference model, its 1984 ISO publication, layer responsibilities, and why TCP/IP displaced the OSI protocols.

title: Internet protocol suite
description: Describes TCP/IP's four layers (link, internet, transport, application), its DARPA origins, and how it differs from the OSI model. Solid undergraduate comparison material.

title: RFC 1122: Requirements for Internet Hosts - Communication Layers
description: Internet Standard specifying what hosts must implement at the link, IP and transport layers, with rationale for each rule. In-depth primary source for the TCP/IP layering model.

title: Data Link Layer in OSI Model - GeeksforGeeks
description: Introduces layer 2 framing and node-to-node delivery, the LLC and MAC sublayers, and the devices and protocols that work at this layer. Accessible entry point.

title: Data link layer
description: Wikipedia article covering frame delivery on a local segment, media access control, frame synchronization, error detection and flow control, with links to specific protocols.

title: Ethernet frame
description: Details the Ethernet frame structure: preamble, source and destination MAC addresses, EtherType, payload and 32-bit CRC checksum. Good for learning a concrete layer 2 format.

title: RFC 826: An Ethernet Address Resolution Protocol
description: Original 1982 ARP specification by David Plummer describing how hosts map IP addresses to 48-bit Ethernet addresses via broadcast requests and caching. Primary source, hence advanced.

title: What is the network layer? | Learning Center
description: Cloudflare explanation of layer 3: moving packets between separate networks, the role of IP, and how this layer is targeted by DDoS attacks. Short beginner introduction.

title: What is routing?
description: Explains how routers choose paths using routing tables, static versus dynamic routes, and protocols such as BGP and OSPF. Fits the routing portion of an undergrad course.

title: Network layer
description: Wikipedia article on layer 3 functions: forwarding, routing, logical addressing, IPv4 fragmentation and reassembly, and protocols like IP, ICMP and OSPF.

title: RFC 791: Internet Protocol
description: The IPv4 standard by Jon Postel, defining addressing, header fields, fragmentation, TTL and checksum. Advanced primary source for the network layer.

title: Transport Layer in OSI Model - GeeksforGeeks
description: Overview of layer 4 functions such as port-based multiplexing, reliability and flow control, with a comparison of TCP, UDP and SCTP and the three-way handshake.

title: Transmission Control Protocol
description: Wikipedia article on TCP covering connection setup, ordered reliable delivery, retransmission, flow control and congestion control. Standard undergraduate depth.

title: User Datagram Protocol
description: Explains connectionless UDP, its header with ports and checksum, and the lack of delivery or ordering guarantees. Useful for contrasting with TCP.

title: RFC 9293: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
description: Current Internet Standard (STD 7) consolidating RFC 793 and later updates, with state machine and segment processing rules. Advanced reference for TCP internals.

title: What is layer 7? | How layer 7 of the Internet works
description: Introduces the application layer as the top OSI layer providing protocols such as HTTP and SMTP to software, plus a note on layer 7 DDoS attacks. Beginner-level.

title: What is DNS? | How DNS works
description: Walks through a DNS lookup from browser and OS cache to recursive resolvers and authoritative nameservers, including caching. Concrete example of an application-layer protocol.

title: HTTP
description: Wikipedia article on the request-response protocol, its evolution through HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, and its messages, methods and status codes.

title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
description: IETF Standards Track specification of HTTP semantics common to all versions: methods, status codes, headers and URI schemes. Advanced normative reference.

title: Java OOP (Object-Oriented Programming)
description: W3Schools introduction to OOP in Java: objects bundle data and behavior and classes act as templates. Short, example-driven and suitable for first-time learners.

title: Lesson: Object-Oriented Programming Concepts
description: Oracle's Java Tutorials lesson introducing objects, classes, inheritance, interfaces and packages using real-world analogies. A solid undergraduate-level conceptual overview.

title: Java OOP(Object Oriented Programming) Concepts - GeeksforGeeks
description: Walks through classes, objects, constructors, abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism with Java code, and weighs the benefits and drawbacks of OOP.

title: Object-oriented programming
description: Wikipedia article covering the history, core features, design principles and criticisms of the OOP paradigm. Suited to learners wanting the broader theory behind the concepts.

title: Java Classes and Objects
description: W3Schools tutorial on defining a Java class, creating objects with new, and organizing code across multiple classes. Simple examples make it a good first stop.

title: Classes (The Java Tutorials)
description: Oracle tutorial page using a Bicycle class to show fields, constructors and methods, plus a MountainBike subclass. Explains how a class declaration is structured.

title: Objects (The Java Tutorials)
description: Oracle tutorial page on creating and using objects with the CreateObjectDemo example, covering instantiation, method calls and cleanup of objects.

title: Chapter 8. Classes (Java Language Specification, Java SE 17)
description: The formal JLS chapter on class declarations, modifiers, inner classes, members, constructors, enums and records. Advanced reading for precise language semantics.

title: Java Encapsulation and Getters and Setters
description: W3Schools tutorial showing how to hide fields with private and expose them via getters and setters, with short code examples for beginners.

title: Controlling Access to Members of a Class
description: Oracle tutorial explaining public, protected, private and package-private access modifiers and why to use the most restrictive level; the core of encapsulation in Java.

title: Abstract Methods and Classes (The Java Tutorials)
description: Oracle tutorial on abstract classes and methods for sharing behavior that subclasses must implement, with a comparison to interfaces to guide design choices.

title: Encapsulation (computer programming)
description: Wikipedia article on encapsulation as a design principle: bundling data with operations and restricting access to support stable interfaces and loose coupling. More theoretical in depth.

title: Java Inheritance (Subclass and Superclass)
description: W3Schools tutorial on extends, subclass and superclass with a Vehicle and Car example, and using final to prevent inheritance. Beginner friendly.

title: Inheritance (The Java Tutorials)
description: Oracle tutorial on what a subclass inherits, constructors and super, overriding versus hiding, and casting within the class hierarchy using a Bicycle example.

title: Inheritance in Java - GeeksforGeeks
description: Explains how a Java class reuses and extends another, covering the types of inheritance and Java's restrictions such as no multiple class inheritance, with examples.

title: Liskov substitution principle
description: Wikipedia article on the Liskov substitution principle: subtypes must be usable wherever supertypes are, covering signature, contract and state constraints. Advanced design reading on correct inheritance.

title: Java Polymorphism
description: W3Schools tutorial showing how subclasses share a method name but behave differently, using an Animal superclass with Pig and Dog subclasses. Very approachable.

title: Polymorphism (The Java Tutorials)
description: Oracle tutorial explaining runtime polymorphism via Bicycle subclasses overriding printDescription, showing virtual method invocation by the actual object type.

title: Polymorphism in Java - GeeksforGeeks
description: Covers compile-time polymorphism (method overloading) and runtime polymorphism (method overriding) in Java with code examples and comparisons.

title: Polymorphism (computer science)
description: Wikipedia article on the theory of polymorphism: ad hoc, parametric and subtype forms across programming languages. Advanced, language-independent perspective.

title: Java Exceptions (Try...Catch)
description: W3Schools tutorial on try, catch, finally and throw for handling runtime errors in Java, with short runnable examples for beginners.

title: Lesson: Exceptions (The Java Tutorials)
description: Oracle lesson on catching, throwing and declaring exceptions, try-with-resources, unchecked exceptions and the advantages of exception handling.

title: Java Exception Handling - GeeksforGeeks
description: Covers the Throwable hierarchy, checked versus unchecked exceptions, try-catch-finally, throw and throws, and custom exceptions with code examples.

title: Chapter 11. Exceptions (Java Language Specification, Java SE 17)
description: The formal JLS chapter defining exception classification, compile-time checking and run-time handling including try/catch/finally semantics. Advanced precise reference.

title: Introduction of DBMS - GeeksforGeeks
description: Beginner-friendly overview of what a DBMS is, its core components, main database types (relational, NoSQL, cloud) and database languages. Good first read before any technical detail.

title: Database
description: Wikipedia overview of databases and database management systems: definitions, history, models, and the functions a DBMS provides. Solid undergraduate-level reference with broad coverage.

title: DBMS - Overview
description: Explains how recorded data becomes information, the features of a modern DBMS, and the kinds of database users. Slightly more structured than an intro, suited to a first course.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: Chapter 51. Overview of PostgreSQL Internals
description: Official docs walking through how a real DBMS processes a query from connection to result (parser, rewriter, planner, executor). Advanced because it exposes DBMS architecture internals.

title: Introduction of ER Model - GeeksforGeeks
description: Introduces entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality and participation constraints, and how to draw ER diagrams. Gentle, example-driven start for beginners.

title: Entity-relationship model
description: Wikipedia article on the ER model covering its concepts, diagram notations and use in conceptual database design. Good undergraduate-level reference on the formalism.

title: DBMS - ER Model Basic Concepts
description: Covers entities, attributes, keys, relationships and mapping cardinalities as the basis of conceptual database design. Medium depth with definitions suited to coursework.

title: The Entity-Relationship Model: Toward a Unified View of Data
description: Peter Chen's original 1976 paper proposing the ER model and showing how network, relational and entity set models derive from it. Hard because it is a primary research source.

title: SQL Zoo
description: Hands-on practice site with graded lessons from basic SELECT through joins and self-joins. Learning by running queries makes it ideal for beginners.

title: Relational model
description: Wikipedia article on Codd's relational model: relations, tuples, keys and the logic-based approach to organizing data. Gives the theory behind SQL at undergraduate level.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: 2.6. Joins Between Tables
description: Official tutorial section on inner, left outer and self joins using the weather and cities example tables. Medium difficulty: assumes basic SELECT knowledge.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: 7.2. Table Expressions
description: Reference-level explanation of how FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING build the virtual table a query operates on, including join types and subqueries. Advanced due to its precise manual style.

title: Introduction to Database Normalization - GeeksforGeeks
description: Explains why splitting data into smaller linked tables reduces redundancy and prevents insert, update and delete anomalies. Accessible starting point before normal forms.

title: Normal Forms in DBMS - GeeksforGeeks
description: Walks through 1NF to 5NF with worked examples and guidance on when to normalize or denormalize. Typical undergraduate-level treatment.

title: Database normalization
description: Wikipedia article on normalization and normal forms introduced by Codd, with the anomalies each form avoids. Good medium-depth reference with formal definitions.

title: A Simple Guide to Five Normal Forms in Relational Database Theory
description: William Kent's classic paper explaining 1NF through 5NF as record-design guidelines for avoiding anomalies. Hard because it covers multivalued and join dependencies up to 5NF.

title: Transaction in DBMS - GeeksforGeeks
description: Explains a transaction as an all-or-nothing group of read/write operations and why it keeps data accurate. Beginner-friendly introduction with simple examples.

title: ACID
description: Wikipedia article on atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability and how they keep data correct despite errors and crashes. Solid undergraduate-level treatment of transaction guarantees.

title: Concurrency Control in DBMS - GeeksforGeeks
description: Covers concurrency problems when transactions overlap, plus locking and timestamp-based protocols and their trade-offs. Medium depth suited to a DBMS course.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: 13.2. Transaction Isolation
description: Official docs on the SQL isolation levels and how PostgreSQL implements Read Committed, Repeatable Read and Serializable, including anomalies and serialization failures. Advanced due to implementation detail.

title: Indexing in Databases - GeeksforGeeks
description: Explains how indexes speed up lookups by storing key values with row pointers, with index types and the cost in storage and write speed. Straightforward intro.

title: Database index
description: Wikipedia article on index data structures, usage and trade-offs such as extra storage and slower writes. Medium-level reference for undergraduates.

title: Anatomy of an SQL Index
description: Use The Index, Luke explains how an index is a sorted structure combining a linked list and a balanced B-tree. Medium difficulty with practical, developer-oriented detail.

title: PostgreSQL Documentation: 11.2. Index Types
description: Official docs on B-tree, Hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN and BRIN indexes and which operators each supports. Advanced because it compares index structures and their use cases.

title: What is Operating System? Tutorial
description: Beginner-friendly Guru99 tutorial on what an OS is, its history, types, functions, kernel and boot process. Plain language and no prerequisites make it a good first read.

title: Operating system
description: Wikipedia overview of OS responsibilities: resource allocation, memory protection, interrupts, file systems and security, plus OS types and history. Solid undergraduate-level survey of the whole field.

title: System call
description: Explains how user programs request kernel services via system calls and traps, and why user and kernel mode separation exists. Suits students who know the basics and want the user/kernel boundary.

title: Introduction to Operating Systems (OSTEP Chapter 2)
description: OSTEP chapter on the OS as a virtualizer of CPU, memory and disk, introducing concurrency and persistence, with a short history of UNIX and Linux. Deeper conceptual framing than typical intro pages.

title: Process vs Thread: Key Differences
description: Short ByteByteGo guide relating programs, processes and threads, contrasting memory isolation, creation cost and communication speed. Quick intro with minimal jargon.

title: The Abstraction: The Process (OSTEP Chapter 4)
description: Covers process machine state, process creation, the running/ready/blocked states and process control blocks. Undergraduate-level treatment with end-of-chapter simulation exercises.

title: Thread (computing)
description: Wikipedia article on threads: kernel, user-level and hybrid models, scheduling, and trade-offs versus processes. Good medium-depth reference for comparing threads and processes.

title: Concurrency: An Introduction (OSTEP Chapter 26)
description: Introduces threads sharing one address space, the thread API motivation, and how unsynchronized updates cause race conditions. In-depth with code traces; advanced for newcomers.

title: CPU Scheduling in Operating System: Types & Algorithms
description: Explains preemptive versus non-preemptive scheduling, scheduling criteria like waiting and response time, and compares FCFS, SJF, Round Robin and multilevel queues with a worked example.

title: Scheduling: Introduction (OSTEP Chapter 7)
description: Walks through FIFO, SJF, STCF and Round Robin using turnaround and response time metrics and shows the trade-off between them. Rigorous yet readable undergraduate treatment.

title: Round-robin scheduling
description: Wikipedia article on round-robin: equal time-slice cycling, starvation avoidance and its fairness trade-offs. Useful medium-level reference on one core algorithm.

title: Scheduling: The Multi-Level Feedback Queue (OSTEP Chapter 8)
description: Detailed treatment of MLFQ rules, priority adjustment, starvation, gaming of the scheduler and priority boosts. Advanced because it builds on basic policies and tackles real design problems.

title: What is Deadlock in Operating System? Explained Simply
description: Plain-language intro to deadlock, the four necessary conditions, and prevention, avoidance (Banker's Algorithm) and detection-and-recovery strategies. Gentle first read.

title: Lecture 8: Deadlock (CS 153, UC Riverside)
description: University lecture slides defining deadlock, the Coffman conditions, resource allocation and waits-for graphs, and comparing ignore, prevention, avoidance and detection strategies.

title: Semaphores (OSTEP Chapter 31)
description: Covers semaphores as locks and ordering tools, the bounded buffer, reader-writer locks and dining philosophers, with code. Solid undergraduate coverage of synchronization primitives.

title: Common Concurrency Problems (OSTEP Chapter 32)
description: Studies real concurrency bugs in MySQL, Apache, Mozilla and OpenOffice, then covers deadlock prevention, avoidance and detection. Advanced because it ties theory to real-world bug data.

title: Paging vs Segmentation
description: Short ByteByteGo comparison of fixed-size paging and variable-size segmentation with address translation steps and pros and cons. Easy entry point to memory management ideas.

title: Memory Management in Operating System
description: Scaler article covering allocation tracking, loading and linking, swapping, contiguous allocation, fragmentation, paging, segmentation and virtual memory in one pass. Solid undergraduate overview.

title: Memory paging
description: Wikipedia article on paging: logical to physical mapping, page faults, replacement algorithms, thrashing, and Windows, Linux and macOS implementations. Medium-depth with real systems.

title: Paging: Introduction (OSTEP Chapter 18)
description: Explains pages and frames, page tables and entry contents, and why naive paging costs memory and speed. Advanced, building on address translation and segmentation chapters.

title: File System in Operating System (OS)
description: Scaler article on how an OS organizes data into files and directories, covering file attributes, access methods, file types and contiguous, indexed and linked allocation. Beginner-friendly.

title: File-System Implementation (TDIU11 lecture notes, Linkoping University)
description: University lecture notes on layered file system structure, directory implementation, allocation methods, free-space management, consistency checking and log-structured file systems.

title: Inode
description: Wikipedia article on inodes: stored attributes, links between file names and inodes, hard links, and fixed versus dynamic inode allocation. Medium-level detail on a core Unix file system structure.

title: File System Implementation (OSTEP Chapter 40)
description: Builds the vsfs file system, with superblock, inodes, bitmaps, data blocks and directories, and traces open, read and write operations and caching. Hard because it requires careful on-disk reasoning.
